summary: John's 2nd cousin 9x removed via Bull Smith (also 3C9R via Topping); Orange County militia colonel and NY state senator — very probably the 'Colonel Woodhull' under whom Thomas Lamoreaux served.
bio:
Commanded the 1st Regiment of Orange County Militia (the Cornwall-area regiment); later NY state senator. SAR record for Thomas Lamoreaux says he served under 'Colonel Woodhull' (first name not given) — so Thomas very probably served under a cousin of his wife Keturah.

Path confirmed in two compiled sources: Bull Smith -> Richard 2d -> Sarah Smith (b. 13 Feb 1700, m. 1716 Nathaniel Woodhull of Mastic) -> Jesse: 2nd cousin 9 times removed (Woodhull Genealogy [R4-S1]; Pelletreau [R4-S3]). The proposed Topping route (via Richard Woodhull II's wife Temperance) is doubtful: the Woodhull Genealogy calls her a Fordham (see Abraham Woodhull). His daughter Hannah (b. 8 Jul 1761) married Oliver Smith of Moriches, a Bull Smith cousin ([R4-S3]).
sources: [R4-S1] Mary Gould Woodhull & Francis Bowes Stevens, Woodhull Genealogy: The Woodhull Family in England and America (1904) (archive.org full text), pp. 62-63, 266 (secondary) https://archive.org/details/woodhullgenealog1904wood

[R4-S3] W. S. Pelletreau (ed.), Records of the Town of Smithtown (1898), Appendix (archive.org full text, scans recordsoftownofs00smitrich and recordstownsmit00pellgoog), App. pp. 465-466, 468 (secondary) https://archive.org/details/recordsoftownofs00smitrich
